dossier.mechanism: AppMeta pulls an app's App Store Connect metadata for all 50 locales into a local snapshot on the Mac. You edit every field side by side against Apple's hard limits: name 30, subtitle 30, promotional text 170, keywords 100, description and What's New 4000. Before anything is pushed, it shows a word-level diff against the last fetched server state, and you push per field, per locale or all at once. It reaches Apple through the ASC API v1 with a .p8 key kept in Keychain. Keyword diagnosis runs on-device; AI is optional, with your own provider.
dossier.audienceScene: An indie iOS/macOS developer with several apps in 10+ locales, at a Mac desk (or on a laptop on a flight) during ship week. This is the journal's 'Friday afternoon App Store Connect block', with Xcode and the ASC web UI open in other windows. They arrive from Google or an AI answer ('app store connect mac app', 'Itsyconnect alternative'). On desktop they are usually already on the Mac they would install it on. On a phone they need to carry the page to that Mac.
dossier.culturalHome: The indie Apple developer scene and App Store Connect's own vocabulary: locales written en-US · de-DE · zh-Hans, 'Ready for Sale', 'Prepare for Submission', What's New, version trains (1.2 → 1.8.1), TestFlight builds, .p8 keys, Fastlane, release notes. Behind it sits the paperwork the job descends from: fields filled inside printed boxes, proofs signed 'OK to print' before press, and the multilingual leaflet folded into every boxed product.
dossier.mustProve: In one viewport: this is a native Mac app (macOS 14+) for App Store Connect. It holds every locale side by side inside Apple's character limits and shows each change before it reaches Apple, demonstrated with real metadata rather than claimed. Keys stay in Keychain, and it talks only to Apple (plus an AI provider you choose). The real price: a free download with demo mode, then $17.99/year or $29.99 lifetime. A working install path: the official badge, and on a phone a way to send the page to the Mac.
dossier.categoryDefault: The dark Mac dev-tool landing page in the Raycast/Linear school: an indigo-violet gradient mesh lifted from the icon, a floating macOS window screenshot with a glow, a 'Download on the Mac App Store' button, an SF-Symbol feature grid, a green-check comparison table and two pricing cards. Its cousin is the terminal-green CLI look used for anything near Fastlane.
dossier.predictableOpposite: Apple-product-page white minimalism: a giant grotesk headline, one centred MacBook render, empty white space and a single blue link. The incumbent cream 'Paper & Ink' template is the other spent option.
dossier.literalReading: 'Meta' read literally means metadata, which leads to the library catalogue card with its fixed fields and subject headings (candidate 6, the only literal one). The icon reads as a networked globe ('global reach'), which no candidate uses.
evidence: _apps/appmeta.md: platforms ['macOS'], status live, price.model freemium, price.value '$17.99/year or $29.99 lifetime'; plans are Annual $17.99/yr and Lifetime $29.99 once (highlight 'Best value') plus plans_footnote; cta_label 'Download Free'; the FAQ confirms a free download with full demo mode (sample data, no developer account needed); macOS 14+; hero.device mac.

Finally native.', secondary, subheadline), quick_answer, who_for 6 / who_not_for 4, alternatives_to 6, founder (Organization, Finland, 4 signals, response time), value_points 4, how_it_works (intro + 7 steps → HowTo), features 8, screenshots 4, comparison_table (6 tools × 13 rows + footnote), plateau_disclosure, training_vocabulary (4 groups), example_insights 4, privacy, faq 16, release (first 2026-02-01, last updated 2026-05-13), related_apps appmeta-pulse + mockly. Absent: spotlight, roadmap, coach_cta, ratings, show_body.

candidates.name: The marked press proof
candidates.why: Every developer has shipped a typo, and the proof signed 'OK to print' is the original 'preview before push'. It carries the word-level diff as standard proofreaders' marks (caret, delete, stet) on real text, and the 11 locales Apple added in 2026 as marked insertions into the 50-code list. Per field, per locale or all becomes what the sign-off covers, and the download is the sign-off box.

candidates.name: The full score versus the players' parts
candidates.why: The ASC web UI hands you one part at a time; AppMeta gives you the score. It carries the 50 locales as braced staves (English variants, Spanish, French, Portuguese and Chinese pairs, and the Indian-region locales as a section). Each bar is a field whose width is its character limit, and pending edits are the conductor's pencil marks. Weakness: at phone width it collapses to a single part, and staff paper drifts toward costume.

candidates.name: The multilingual leaflet in the product box
candidates.why: The same text repeated under 'EN · DA · DE …' tabs is exactly what a 50-locale listing is. It carries the locales as a reversed code-tab index (navigation and proof at once) and puts real panels of one release note side by side with their counts. The specifications, 'not included' and manufacturer panels hold the field limits, the plateau disclosure and the founder. It is weaker on the diff, which has to be shown inside one panel.

candidates.name: The comb-field form in drop-out ink
candidates.why: One box per letter makes Apple's limits physical: 30 boxes for name and subtitle, 100 for keywords. It carries the character budget (AppMeta's real subtitle fills 29 of 30 boxes) and the diff as the printed correction rule: strike through, write above, initial. Push granularity becomes tick boxes and the push becomes the signed declaration. The red drop-out ink is Apple's structure and the black is your entry. Finland's forms are bilingual, as AppMeta's locales are.

candidates.name: The engineering drawing sheet and its revision block
candidates.why: Revision clouds and delta triangles are a hand-drawn diff, and the revision table is the version train (1.2 → 1.8.1, 'Ready for Sale'). 'Sheet 1 of 50' carries the locales, the title block's fixed fields carry the limits, and 'Approved for release' is the push. Weakness: blueprint is a cliché, and drafting is not the indie developer's world.

candidates.name: The library catalogue card drawer
candidates.why: A catalogue card is metadata in its original form: fixed fields, subject headings as keywords, one card per locale in a drawer of 50, and a 'withdrawn / replaced' stamp for the diff. It is the literal reading and warm-bookish (cream card stock is the spent prior), and it is weak on the diff and on the Mac.

candidates.name: The broadcast mixing console
candidates.why: Fifty channel strips side by side, with tape scribble-strips reading de-DE and fr-FR. You solo one locale, pre-fade listen is the preview, and nothing reaches the master bus (Apple) until you push the fader. Strong on side-by-side and preview, but it drifts toward dark hardware and LEDs and sits next to MediaKit's rack.

styles.label: One Box Per Letter
styles.lineage: Comb-field forms in drop-out ink. On OCR forms the boxes and labels are printed in red drop-out ink so the scanner reads only the black entries (the IRS 'Copy A' convention). Tax returns and landing cards use one box per character. Finland's bilingual Finnish/Swedish official forms carry the printed correction rule: strike through, write the correct entry above, initial.
styles.thesis: The page is a form whose boxes are Apple's real field limits (30 for name, 30 for subtitle, 100 for keywords), printed in drop-out red, with AppMeta's own metadata typed in black. The character budget, the correction (the diff) and the signed declaration (the push) are its working parts. It refuses the dark dev-tool landing page with a floating Mac window.
styles.scene: An indie developer at the Mac in office daylight during ship week, filling the same fields for the twelfth locale. White bond paper, one scheme (color-scheme: light).

type.utility: Courier Prime 400/700 (18.6 + 19.3 KB), used only for typed entries inside comb fields and their counts ('29/30'). This is real character-counted data at one glyph per box, and AppMeta's own field editors are monospaced too.
type.rationale: Finlandica is Helsinki Type Studio's 2021 grotesk for Finland's country brand. Its crossed 7 comes from Nordic handwriting, and its narrow proportions fit labels into tight boxes, so it reads as the Finnish public form this Finnish studio actually fills in. No sibling world uses it. Courier Prime is the typewriter that filled forms before the web, and mono appears only where each character occupies one counted box. About 61 KB in total.

styles.navigation: The form head carries the parts index as red underlined Finlandica 600 links (Fields · Corrections · Locales · Procedure · Fees · Notes), each pointing to a part-band id. On mobile a text button labelled 'Parts' (no hamburger glyph) opens the same list as a full-width ruled column under the head. Every part band ends at right with 'Back to top of form'. Lagerland appears only in the shared footer strip.
styles.signatureInteraction: 'Try the Subtitle field'. A real <input> styled as a 30-box comb: Courier Prime, letter-spacing matched to a repeating-linear-gradient box grid, placeholder 'App Store Connect, done right', and aria-describedby pointing at the count. The HTML ships maxlength=30; about 30 lines of JS raise it to 40, update the typed count ('29/30') and set a CSS variable that tints the overflow boxes. Past 30 it prints 'Over by 8: App Store Connect will not accept this. AppMeta flags it before you push.' Nothing is submitted or sent. No-JS: the comb still takes typing up to 30 characters, and the static 7/30 and 29/30 rows carry the point. Reduced motion: there is no motion to remove; colour changes are instant.
styles.motionGrammar: Paper holds still. Entries are present on load with no typing animation, so content is never hidden. Comb boxes darken their stroke on hover and focus (no movement). The return slip slides up 64px in 160ms ease-out when it first appears. Anchor jumps scroll smoothly. Reduced motion removes the slide and the smooth scroll. No scroll reveals.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy becomes a 'Data protection notice' form: the same head and red part bands, with a calm reading column of Finlandica 400 18px black on bond white at 66ch for overview, collection, storage, third parties, children and changes. Above it, typed fact boxes ('Data collected: none', 'Tracking: no', 'Account: your own ASC API key') link to the transparency row. Support becomes a 'Request for assistance' form: a mailto link whose prefilled body lists what to include (app version, macOS version, what happened), the response time, and no web form that collects anything. /alternatives/app-store-connect-web/ becomes a 'Comparison of forms': a two-column ruled table (AppMeta vs ASC web on speed, localisation, safety, credentials), the 'Pick AppMeta if' and 'Stick with ASC web if' lists as tick lists, FAQ notes, and a closing declaration with the badge.
styles.assetsNeeded: None new: it runs on the icon, the four landscape screenshots, the QR and 11.png's real entry text. Recommended production task: Apple's official 'Download on the Mac App Store' badge artwork to replace the iOS badge on Mac-only pages.
styles.risk: Forms carry friction: the page could read as more paperwork rather than relief, and full-commitment red on white can tip into alarm. Red must stay apparatus and never mean 'error'; the black typed data carries the warmth. Combs must be pin-sharp at every size, because a sloppy box grid kills the idea. The mobile comb wrap (15 boxes per row) needs careful tuning so words do not break unreadably.
styles.memoryTest: The AppMeta page was a red tax-style form. Its subtitle filled 29 of 30 boxes, and when I typed my own subtitle in, the boxes went red at 31.

specimen.sub: App Store Connect, native on your Mac.

fixes.text: Re-derive every visitorPath from the world's own reading order, and enforce two rules. (1) Within a surface, no two styles may share the relative order of more than two of {price, screenshots, comparison, privacy record, founder, FAQ}. (2) At least one style per surface must change GROUPING, not just order: for example, FAQ split into the sections it answers, who_for/who_not_for folded into the price, or the privacy record as the opener. World-native examples: tare-b sets Puzzle No. 1 before the Rules and puts price and answers at the back like a book. studio-a, allpaid-c and rightsplit-a open with the record (bin label, statement, label data) before any feature. soon-b prints the fare and stub (price) on the face, first. gymlogger-x-c shows the plateau formula before any offer. xiangqiful-c files each FAQ as a margin question on the entry it concerns. observa-b ends on 'past issues' (release notes) instead of a closing CTA block. The maker/freshness line and the shared footer strip may stay common.

Add one production task to every style: a one-off script in scripts/ (already excluded from the build, so it is not a deploy build step) that commits derivatives. Icons at 64, 128 and 256px (WebP plus a PNG fallback, about 15 KB or less at 128). Screenshots at 400w, 800w and 1200w WebP (about 40, 90 and 160 KB or less). The studio mark as the clean SVG that studio a/b/c already ask for. Front matter keeps the original paths; one include maps them to the derivatives and emits width/height, srcset/sizes, loading=lazy and decoding=async (eager plus fetchpriority=high only for a single hero image).

Make it a global contract: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-top); scroll-padding-bottom: var(--sticky-bottom) }, so focus and anchors never land under a bar. Allow one sticky element per edge, pad the bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and on viewports shorter than 600px hide the top strip while the bottom bar is showing.

styles.label: Passed for Press
styles.lineage: The prepress proof. Linotype and Monotype galley proofs were marked with standard proofreaders' marks (BS 5261-2 / Chicago Manual of Style: caret, delete, stet, transpose, the 'Qy' query). The Dylux blueline was the final contact proof, printed entirely in one blue, which the client signed 'OK to print' before plates were made.
styles.thesis: The page is one long galley proof of AppMeta's own App Store copy, printed in blueline blue, with its changes marked in the margins and a sign-off box that is the download. 'See every change before it goes to Apple' becomes the way the page is read rather than a feature bullet. It refuses the dark landing page with a glowing window screenshot.
styles.scene: A developer at the Mac the afternoon before a release, checking the last proof before anything goes to Apple: a blueline sheet under even daylight. One light scheme (color-scheme: light), with the ground tinted blue so the page reads drenched rather than white.

type.utility: None. Counts and limits use Charis lining figures; there is no mono.
type.rationale: Charis SIL is SIL's open extension of Bitstream Charter, which Matthew Carter drew in 1987 to stay crisp on the 300-dpi laser printers that ran off proofs. macOS bundles Charter, so @font-face lists local('Charter') before the self-hosted file and Mac visitors download nothing, a fitting answer to 'Finally native'. Its sturdy, low-contrast serifs and the rule of no italic at display size keep it out of the high-contrast editorial cluster. About 69 KB in total, near zero on a Mac.

styles.navigation: The job docket carries the contents (Locales · Fields · Price · Queries) as underlined blue Charis links, with the 'Show marks / As printed' toggle beside them. Margin side-heads label every section, and each section ends with 'Back to the head of the galley'. On mobile a 'Contents' text button opens the list under the docket, and side-heads move inline above their paragraphs at 17px 700.
styles.signatureInteraction: 'Show marks / As printed'. One toggle switches every marked galley between the marked proof and the clean printed line, mirroring AppMeta's diff preview against the pushed state: <del> collapses, <ins> drops into the line in blue type, and the marks and marginal notes fade. A small class toggle in JS keeps state in the URL hash. No-JS: the marked proof shows, and each marked passage is followed by its server-rendered 'As printed' line, so both states are in the HTML. Reduced motion: the swap is instant, with no fade and no mark drawing.
styles.motionGrammar: Only the pencil moves. When a marked passage first enters view, its SVG marks draw on (stroke-dashoffset, 400ms, staggered 60ms) under html.js; the text never moves and is visible throughout. The toggle cross-fades marks in 200ms. The slug strip slides up in 160ms. Reduced motion shows the marks already drawn and makes every swap instant. No scroll reveals of text.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy and support pages are 'Imprint' galleys: the same blue sheet and docket, and a calm reading column of 66ch Charis 400 19px blue on the tinted sheet (10:1) with side-heads in the margin. They carry no proof marks except one stamp, 'Data collected: none', linking to /transparency/#appmeta. Support is 'Queries to the printer': a mailto link with prefilled subject and body, plus the response time. /alternatives/app-store-connect-web/ is a two-proof comparison: AppMeta and the ASC web UI as facing columns on the galley (stacked on mobile) with the differences marked, the FAQ set as queries, and the sign-off box with the badge.
styles.assetsNeeded: None. The marks are hand-coded inline SVG paths, and the page runs on the existing icon, screenshots and QR. Recommended: Apple's 'Download on the Mac App Store' badge artwork.
styles.risk: Honest familiarity: a paper proof sits close to the print/editorial register AI pages drift toward. It avoids italic display and mono labels, but a weak build becomes a blue blog post. An all-blue page can feel cold and monotonous, and the screenshots are its only colour. Many developers do not know proof marks, so every mark needs a plain-language note beside it.
styles.memoryTest: The AppMeta page was one long blue proof sheet with pencil marks. The 11 new locales were marked in like corrections, and the download was a box that said 'OK to print'.

fixes.text: Re-derive every visitorPath from the world's own reading order, and enforce two rules. (1) Within a surface, no two styles may share the relative order of more than two of {price, screenshots, comparison, privacy record, founder, FAQ}. (2) At least one style per surface must change GROUPING, not just order: for example, FAQ split into the sections it answers, who_for/who_not_for folded into the price, or the privacy record as the opener. World-native examples: tare-b sets Puzzle No. 1 before the Rules and puts price and answers at the back like a book. studio-a, allpaid-c and rightsplit-a open with the record (bin label, statement, label data) before any feature. soon-b prints the fare and stub (price) on the face, first. gymlogger-x-c shows the plateau formula before any offer. xiangqiful-c files each FAQ as a margin question on the entry it concerns. observa-b ends on 'past issues' (release notes) instead of a closing CTA block. The maker/freshness line and the shared footer strip may stay common.

Keep proof marks and the sign-off box on appmeta-b, because marked text changes are AppMeta's mechanism. mockly-b keeps imposition, crop marks, the colour bar and ganged trims. It moves the action into the press-run dispatch docket on the gripper edge (no 'OK to upload' approval box, no signature line) and drops the magenta proof-query circles. Caveats go into the slug lines.

Add one production task to every style: a one-off script in scripts/ (already excluded from the build, so it is not a deploy build step) that commits derivatives. Icons at 64, 128 and 256px (WebP plus a PNG fallback, about 15 KB or less at 128). Screenshots at 400w, 800w and 1200w WebP (about 40, 90 and 160 KB or less). The studio mark as the clean SVG that studio a/b/c already ask for. Front matter keeps the original paths; one include maps them to the derivatives and emits width/height, srcset/sizes, loading=lazy and decoding=async (eager plus fetchpriority=high only for a single hero image).

Make it a global contract: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-top); scroll-padding-bottom: var(--sticky-bottom) }, so focus and anchors never land under a bar. Allow one sticky element per edge, pad the bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and on viewports shorter than 600px hide the top strip while the bottom bar is showing.

Anchor each mark to the markup that carries the change. Strike lines are text-decoration on <del>, drawn on with a background-size wipe. Carets and insertion marks are ::before/::after on <ins>. Margin notes are floated <aside> elements tied to their passage. Drive the passages from front matter (before and after strings), so the diff and both states render from data.

styles.label: The Fifty-Language Leaflet
styles.lineage: The multilingual instruction leaflet folded into every boxed device. Its cover carries a language index of reversed code tabs ('EN · DA · DE · ES · FI · FR …'), and the same text repeats per language under each tab. It is set in a wide-coverage sans on thin 40–60 gsm paper where the reverse shows through, with a specifications table, a 'not included' line and the manufacturer block on the back panel.
styles.thesis: An App Store listing is a fifty-language leaflet, and AppMeta edits every panel side by side. So the page opens on the full index of the 50 ASC locale codes as both its navigation and its proof, with three real panels of one release note next to each other. It refuses the single-window screenshot hero.
styles.scene: The developer at the Mac in daylight, unfolding a release in every language at once: thin printed paper on a desk. One light scheme (color-scheme: light).

styles.navigation: The leaflet's own index is the navigation. The header carries Contents links named after the panels. On desktop a thumb index of reversed tabs (Index · Box · Start · Specs · Price · Data · Questions) is fixed to the right edge, with the current panel's tab turned violet by IntersectionObserver; without JS they are plain anchor links. On mobile a 'Contents' text button opens the panel list. The 50 locale tabs link into the Languages panel.
styles.signatureInteraction: 'The language index'. Tapping, hovering or focusing any of the 50 code tabs fills a single card under the grid with that locale's English name, its endonym in its own script, and whether Apple added it in 2026. All of this is real data, server-rendered in the Languages panel, which JS clones into the card. No-JS: each tab is an anchor to its Languages row, and :target highlights the row in violet. Reduced motion: the card swaps instantly.
styles.motionGrammar: Folds never animate. Only the tabs respond: on hover or focus a tab lifts 2px and inverts in 120ms. The index card cross-fades in 150ms, and the folded-edge strip slides up in 160ms. Reduced motion removes the lift and makes swaps instant. No scroll reveals.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy is the 'Safety and data' leaflet: the same paper, header and creases, a reversed tab heading 'Privacy', and a calm reading column of Noto 400 18px at 68ch. A key-facts table (data collected: none · tracking: no · account: none · network: App Store Connect API) links to the transparency record. Support is the 'Service and support' panel: a mailto link with a prefilled body, the response time and FAQ links. /alternatives/app-store-connect-web/ is a 'Comparable products' leaflet: a two-column AppMeta vs ASC web specification panel, the 'pick if' and 'stick with if' lists, the FAQ, and a back cover with the badge.
styles.assetsNeeded: None. It is entirely typographic, using the icon, screenshots, QR and the real text read from 1.png. Recommended: Apple's 'Download on the Mac App Store' badge artwork.
styles.risk: Fifty reversed tabs can read as a heavy wall of codes, though this audience lives in these codes. The instruction-leaflet register risks feeling like a manual rather than a pitch, so the cover panel has to sell. Endonyms depend on system script fonts. The real multi-locale text is GymLogger X's, not AppMeta's own, and must be labelled plainly. All three rolled worlds are paper, so this one leans on its index topology and the app's own violet to stand apart.
styles.memoryTest: The AppMeta page opened on a grid of fifty little black language tabs with eleven in purple, and three real release notes side by side, like the leaflet in a new phone box.

canon: Canon (the standing exit, never recommended): the dark Mac dev-tool landing page played straight. It has an indigo-to-violet mesh from the icon, a floating macOS window screenshot with a soft glow, a centred headline and a 'Download on the Mac App Store' button. Below sit a 3×3 feature grid with SF-Symbol-style icons, a green-check comparison table and two pricing cards with Lifetime highlighted, polished to Raycast's level.
notes: The roll ran degraded (roll service unreachable; no catalog challengers and no quality-bar boards). The dealt index binds anyway. Seed key 41d3588d, assigned 4; re-roll 1 dealt 3, which is distinct, so there was no further re-roll. Neither dealt index is 1, so B is my top-ranked candidate as IMPECCABLE’S PICK. All three dealt worlds are paper families (form, proof, leaflet), and nothing factual justified a re-roll. They are separated by topology (a boxed 12-column form grid; one long galley with working margins; a cover panel plus a code-tab index and concertina panels), colour strategy (Committed drop-out red; Drenched blueline blue; Restrained black plus the app's violet) and type (Finlandica + Courier Prime; Charis SIL/Charter; Noto Sans variable). They also map AppMeta's own pipeline: enter the fields (A), check the diff (B), publish in every language (C). All three are light because each scene is paper at a daylight desk; none is forced dark. Fonts were verified on Fontsource (finlandica 400/700, courier-prime 400/700, charis-sil 400/700/400i, @fontsource-variable/noto-sans wdth+wght). Sizes: A ≈ 61 KB, B ≈ 69 KB (zero on Macs via local Charter), C ≈ 60 KB. Charis SIL's Fontsource subset has no small caps (smcp), so none are specified. Things the owner should know: (1) Screenshot alts 2–4 do not match the images: 2.png is the In-App Purchases editor, 3.png is TestFlight, and 4.png is the Localizations editor. No screenshot shows the diff preview, keyword optimizer or AI picker, so every style draws the diff typographically and captions each image with what it shows. 1.png shows real GymLogger X 1.8.1 notes in en-US, Danish and German, used as labelled real material. (2) 11–14.png are 1280×800 App Store marketing images. Only 11.png's visible entry text (AppMeta 7/30; 'App Store Connect, done right' 29/30) is used, as data. (3) The existing badge include is the iOS 'Download on the App Store' artwork. A Mac-only page should use Apple's official 'Download on the Mac App Store' badge; that is a production task. (4) The transparency row says network calls go to 'Apple App Store Connect API only. No other endpoints', but the app page says a configured AI provider is also contacted; align the record. (5) app_enrichment.yml says 'no subscription' while the Annual plan renews ('Cancel anytime'); styles follow plans and price.value. (6) hero.secondary and the founder heading hard-code '19 apps'. Copy the styles own uses computed counts, but those literals need syncing. (7) The copy calls all 11 new locales 'Indian-region', but Slovenian is not; styles say '11 added in 2026'. (8) There is no version field in the front matter, so the maker line shows first released and last updated only. (9) Only /alternatives/app-store-connect-web/ targets AppMeta; the other five alternatives_to names stay unlinked. (10) example_insights card 4 cites a 'Storefront Intelligence dataset'; verify it before rendering. (11) For a Mac-only app the QR is secondary. Phone visitors (who cannot install a Mac app) get 'Send this page to your Mac' via navigator.share (AirDrop or Handoff), with a mailto fallback; this is a site feature, not an app claim. (12) show_body is not set; the markdown body is available if the owner wants an About block.

pageFixes.issue: Below the hero, the three styles of each surface follow one section order with new labels. appmeta-a ≡ appmeta-b, gymlogger-x-a ≡ -b ≡ -c, rightsplit-b ≡ -c, shogiful-b ≡ -c, wanderwiki-a ≡ -b (-c swaps two blocks) and pawza-a ≡ -c. The xiangqiful, earnlock and millrace trios each differ by one swap. Across the 60 microsite styles, one order dominates: hero → quick answer → (quick reference) → how it works → screenshots → features → who_for/who_not_for → price → comparison → privacy → founder/about → (roadmap) → FAQ → further reading → closing. That is one static structure in 60 costumes, which is the thing the owner refused ('do not use the same static structure for each page, build them from scratch'). It also makes the three styles per page skin choices, not page choices.
